Why is the sky blue?

Not a reflection of the sea
Not the colour of space: space is black
Same sunlight. Same air.
What changes is how much air it crosses
Sunlight is every colour mixed
Each colour has its own wavelength

Blue: shorter waves
In space they travel together
Then the light reaches the air
Air: nitrogen and oxygen molecules
Over 1,000 times smaller than the wave
The wave shakes the electrons
The molecule sends light back out
This is scattering
The light is not absorbed
It keeps its colour
It only changes direction
Not every colour scatters equally
Shorter wave, faster shake, more light
Half the wavelength: 16× the scattering
Blue scatters about 6× more than red
Straight down through the atmosphere
Rayleigh scattering
Lord Rayleigh, 1871
Air molecules alone are enough (Einstein)

Sunlight streams through the air
Molecules scatter a little toward you
Mostly blue

Scattered again and again: colours remix
Less air above you: a darker sky

1. The sun gives off less violet

The mix reads as blue
